mappings.note: Asks the student to throw light on the line 'हरि आप हरो जन री भीर'. Explicating a quoted line is भाव-पक्ष व्याख्या, so LO-5 rather than LO-4's content recall.
Stem says 'पंक्ति पर भाव प्रकट करें' for the Gajraj couplet -- the भाव is named as the deliverable, which is LO-5 and not LO-4.
Asks what Meera is saying in the quoted line 'चाकरी में दरसण पास्यूँ...'. A paraphrase of the poet's own words = LO-5; the same fact asked without the quotation would have been LO-4.
Whose sari Krishna kept extending (द्रौपदी) -- the first pad's allusion recalled as fact. LO-4, not LO-5.
The advantages of staying near Krishna that the second pad lists. Content comprehension, so LO-4 rather than LO-5.
Asks which भाव the पद express (कृष्ण-भक्ति भाव). Naming the emotive register is exactly LO-5; LO-4 would claim a factual recall that is not what is tested.
What she wants to build for Krishna to walk in (बाग-बगीचे). Detail of the second pad, LO-4 and not LO-5.
Where Krishna grazes cattle and charms everyone (वृंदावन). Place named in the pad, so LO-4.
Whom Krishna killed to save the elephant (मगरमच्छ) -- the Gajendra allusion as narrative fact. LO-4; the item that asks the भाव of the same couplet is separately mapped LO-5.
तात्पर्य of 'ऊँचा-ऊँचा महल बणावं बिच-बिच राखू बारी'. Construing a quoted line = LO-5, not LO-4.
Who saved Draupadi's honour (श्रीकृष्ण). Plain recall of the pad's allusion, LO-4 rather than LO-5.
Whom the poet's word 'हरि' denotes (Vishnu and his avatars). This is a gloss on Meera's diction, i.e. कला-पक्ष -- LO-5, not the content outcome LO-4.
What she wants as wages (दर्शन). Stated in the second pad, so LO-4 rather than LO-5.
What kind of जागीर she seeks (भाव-भक्ति रूपी). Recall from the pad; the separate item asking why भक्ति is *called* a जागीर is the LO-5 one.
The meeting place she chose (यमुना किनारा). Content recall, LO-4 and not LO-5.
Gloss of the word 'चीर' (= वस्त्र). Word-level explanation of the poet's language, hence LO-5 rather than LO-4.
Why Krishna took the नरहरि form -- to protect his devotee, as the allusion in the pad holds. A reason at content level, so LO-4 not LO-5.
Whose दासी Meera calls herself (गिरधारी लाल). The pad's own signature line, recalled as fact -- LO-4.
What she requests in the second pad (to be kept as a चाकर). Content comprehension, LO-4 and not LO-5.
What she would do for Krishna as a चाकर (build a palace, plant a garden). Both are stated in the pad, so LO-4.
What she wants to do in Vrindavan's lanes (sing his लीला). Content of the pad, LO-4 rather than LO-5.
Asks which भावना the line 'छाडि़ दयी कुल की कानि' expresses (a challenge to society). The deliverable is the named feeling behind a quoted line, so LO-5, not LO-4.
In whose company she abandoned लोक-लाज (संतों). A fact stated in the पद, so LO-4 rather than the interpretive LO-5.
Which creeper she sowed (प्रेम की बेल). The image is recalled, not explained, so LO-4; an item asking what the बेल stands for would be LO-5.
What she watered the प्रेम-बेलि with (आँसुओं से). Recall of the pad's wording, LO-4 and not LO-5.
What sight gladdens her in the world (प्रभु-भक्ति). Content of the pad, so LO-4.
Whose दासी she accepts herself to be (श्रीकृष्ण). Factual recall from the pad -- LO-4, not LO-5.
What sight makes her weep (जगत). Direct comprehension, so LO-4 rather than LO-5.
Before whom she danced (श्रीकृष्ण की मूर्ति). Content of the pad, LO-4.
What people called Meera (बावरी) -- the pad states it. LO-4, not LO-5; no feeling or device is asked to be named.
What her न्यात thought her (कुलनासी). Recall of the pad's word in context, so LO-4.
Who sent the cup of poison. An event narrated in the pad, so LO-4 rather than the poet-biography competency C-H2.3, which is reserved for facts outside the verse.
What Meera did on drinking the poison (हँसती रही). Content of the pad, LO-4 and not LO-5.
By what name she calls her lord (गिरधर नागर). Recall of the poem's address, not a gloss of it, so LO-4.
What her lord is said to be (अविनासी). The pad's own epithet recalled, so LO-4 rather than LO-5.
Asks which भावना the two pads together express (भक्ति-भावना). Characterising the emotive content of the poems is LO-5, not the content recall of LO-4.
Asks the distinguishing quality of Meera's भक्ति (uninitiated, heart-born, surrendered). That is a statement about the भाव-पक्ष of her verse, so LO-5 rather than LO-4.
Why her पद centre on प्रेम -- an argument about the poems' governing emotion. भाव-पक्ष, hence LO-5; LO-4 would fit only a factual answer from the text.
Why she wants to wear the कुसुंबी sari. A motive at content level (to meet and please Krishna), so LO-4 -- unlike the sibling item that asks the तात्पर्य of the word 'कुसुम्बी', which is LO-5.
Why her भाव-भक्ति is called a 'जागीर' -- construing the poet's metaphor. That is कला-पक्ष व्याख्या (LO-5); the item merely asking which जागीर she wants is LO-4.
Asks in what form the poet has described Krishna's beauty. The deliverable is the manner of depiction (मोर मुकुट, वैजयंती, पीतांबर as a portrait), i.e. कला-पक्ष -- LO-5, not LO-4.
Asks only for the poem's and poet's names -- a text-identification item. Neither LO-4 (काव्यबोध) nor LO-5 (भाव/कला) is being tested, so the literature competency is the honest citation.
Why Meera desires Krishna's चाकरी, a 3-mark answer built from what the second pad states (nearness, daily darshan, remembrance). LO-4; no भाव or shaili term is demanded, so not LO-5.
How the poet has described Krishna's रूप-सौंदर्य -- the question is about the depiction itself, so कला-पक्ष and LO-5, not the content outcome LO-4.
Why she wants darshan at midnight by the Yamuna. A motive drawn from the pad's situation, so LO-4 rather than LO-5, which is kept for glosses and for naming भाव/शैली.
Which स्वरूप of Krishna Meera has imagined -- the question is about her poetic कल्पना and its imagery, hence LO-5 rather than LO-4.
How she seeks to end her heart's अधीरता -- by pleading for darshan, as the pad says. Content-level answer, so LO-4 and not LO-5.
How and why Krishna helped Gajraj, explicitly 'पद के आधार पर'. The allusion is retold as narrative, so LO-4; the item asking the भाव of the same couplet is LO-5.
How Meera frames the plea to remove her suffering -- by listing the devotees already rescued. The pad's own argument, so LO-4 rather than LO-5.
Whose चाकरी she wants and why. Content comprehension of the second pad, LO-4 and not LO-5.
Describe the efforts Meera makes for Krishna, in the student's own words. The substance is drawn from the pads' content, so LO-4; nothing about craft or feeling is named, so not LO-5.
Quotes the चाकरी stanza and asks the दास्य भक्ति in it to be made clear. Naming and explaining the devotional mode of a quoted passage is भाव-पक्ष व्याख्या -- LO-5, not LO-4.
Stem is literally 'भाव स्पष्ट करें' on the closing couplet. That is the LO-5 deliverable; LO-4 would be right only if the allusion's facts were asked.
Describe the नरसिंह form -- the Hiranyakashyap/Prahlad narrative the pad alludes to. Mythological content, so LO-4 and not the कला-पक्ष outcome LO-5.
Which three things the pad gives special weight to (दर्शन, स्मरण, भाव-भक्ति). A list drawn from the text, so LO-4; the item asking the भावार्थ of 'तीनूं बातां सरसी' is the LO-5 one.
The significance of the Yamuna bank in the pad -- answered from what the text and its Krishna lore supply (flute, raas, meeting place). Content, so LO-4 rather than LO-5.
Write on Meera's भाषा-शैली. Style and language are the कला-पक्ष, so LO-5; LO-4 would wrongly claim content comprehension.

Two-part 5-mark item: name the भक्त-भगवान relationship Meera claims with Krishna (भाव-पक्ष, LO-5) and then retell one of the rescues she cites (content, LO-4). Both halves carry marks, so both are cited rather than forcing one.
Throw light on Meera's भाषा-शैली at 5 marks -- Brij mixed with Rajasthani, माधुर्य गुण, अलंकार. Squarely कला-पक्ष, hence LO-5 and not LO-4.
Asks what kind her भक्ति-भावना is (शृंगार-प्रधान, दास्य in the second pad). Characterising the emotive mode is LO-5; LO-4 is for facts the pads state.
